visual.general_description: Three axial chest CT slices (lung window) from the index patient showing a right-sided opacity and its resolution.
visual.detailed_description: Panel A: Axial lung-window CT through the heart. In the right lung (image left) a wedge of patchy, ill-defined increased density extends from the hilum toward the lateral chest wall, with a white arrow pointing to its medial part. The left lung (image right) appears clear apart from vessels; a small L orientation marker sits at the right edge of the panel. Panel B: Axial lung-window CT at a slightly different level. A linear/patchy density near the right hilum is marked by a white arrow; it is much smaller than in panel A. Both lungs are otherwise aerated. A small L marker sits at the right edge. Panel C: Axial lung-window CT. The lungs are aerated with visible vessels; no discrete arrow is present and the previously dense right hilar opacity is not evident at this window. A small L marker sits at the right edge.

visual.general_description: Six axial chest CT slices (lung window) from the index patient across the immune-related pneumonitis course.
visual.detailed_description: Panel A: Axial lung-window CT through the heart. Both lungs are aerated with normal-appearing vessels; no arrow or focal opacity is marked. Small L marker at the right edge. Panel B: Axial lung-window CT. A white arrow points at a patchy hazy density in the right lower lung (image left) near the posterior pleura; scattered mild ground-glass density is also seen in both lungs. Small L marker at the right edge. Panel C: Axial lung-window CT without arrows; the lungs are mostly clear with a faint peripheral hazy density in the right posterior lung and visible vessels. Small L marker at the right edge. Panel D: Axial lung-window CT. Two white arrows mark patchy hazy opacities in the right lung (one near the right hilum anteriorly, one in the right lower lobe posteriorly); the left lung shows milder haze. Small L marker at the right edge. Panel E: Axial lung-window CT. Three white arrows mark widespread patchy opacities: right anterior, right posterior lower, and left lateral lung; extent is greater than in panel D. Small L marker at the right edge. Panel F: Axial lung-window CT. One white arrow marks a patchy density in the right anterior lung; the remaining lungs show mild patchy haze. Small L marker at the right edge.
